result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A groups its content better: the trip name and date sit close together, a full-width divider separates the details from the line items, and the total gets its own rule and a larger gap. B puts a rule under every line item, so the items and the total read as evenly spaced rows; its tinted date box is a nice touch, though. Both have good padding (about 24–28 px), right-aligned prices and a low-emphasis Change dates link. Both buttons measure about 50 px tall, slightly over the 48 px limit, which costs each a point on item 2. The CSS isn't visible in the screenshots, so item 4 is estimated from the rendered spacing. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both cards have comfortable padding, a prominent teal button and a low-emphasis Change dates link. Both buttons measure about 49–50 px tall in the screenshots, slightly above the 48 px limit. B groups the content more clearly: the title sits close to its date and time, the line items sit tight together, and a rule plus a larger gap sets off the total. In A, a rule separates every line item, so the total reads more like one more evenly spaced row. Item 4 is scored from the screenshots only, since the CSS wasn't available.
